physicalNotes: Radius 0.13560555 Jupiter radii from Castro-González et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..52C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A..52C/abstract): 9,694.7 km at 71,492 km per Jupiter radius. GM from the mass 0.00843222 Jupiter masses (Castro-González et al. 2023, the mass the NASA Exoplanet Archive's composite table adopts (2023A&A...675A..52C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023A&A...675A..52C/abstract) times JPL's Jupiter GM. A sphere: no oblateness is measured.

sources.period: Oddo et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..134O), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ODDO_ET_AL__2023): P 7.39726 d
sources.shape: Castro-González et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..52C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2023): a/R* 28.1; Castro-González et al. 2023 (2023A&A...675A..52C), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname CASTRO_GONZALEZ_ET_AL_2023): inclination 88.32 degrees
sources.eccentricity: No archive row states an eccentricity; the orbit is taken as circular
sources.phase: Oddo et al. 2023 (2023AJ....165..134O), via the NASA Exoplanet Archive ps table (pl_refname ODDO_ET_AL__2023): transit mid-time 2459489.1482 BJD, taken as BJD_TDB; with its period, the row that predicts 2026-01-01 best (1 sigma 7 min)
sources.orientation: Display convention: transit photometry does not measure the orbit's position angle on the sky, so the ascending node is set at position angle 0 (celestial north).
